A Markdown linearity test compares time at two sizes instead of against a wall-clock budget (rich-unfiled-791c.kulj) (#452)

* A Markdown linearity test compares time at two sizes instead of against a wall-clock budget (rich-unfiled-791c.kulj)

The definition test parsed 200 000 lines against a 2 s budget; linear took
0.9 s alone and crossed 2 s once under a loaded full suite. expectLinearTime
(test/suite/linear-time.ts) times the work at n and 4n, fastest of three each,
and requires under 8x: the real parse grows 4.0x, the quadratic one it was
written against (definitionAt's line runs not doubling) 14x at 25 000 lines.

* expectLinearTime reads the median ratio of back-to-back pairs and refuses a size too small to measure (rich-unfiled-791c.kulj)

A separate fastest run per size let a load that arrived after the first
small run inflate every large run: the ratio read the step, not the work.
Pairing cancels a load within each pair, and the median drops the one pair
a step or stall lands across, in either direction. A floor on the smaller
run's time fails a size where fixed costs would pass quadratic work.

* vitest.config.ts states the complexity-guard rule as a rule, not as what every guard already does (rich-unfiled-791c.kulj)
